topLine: A quiet day in NSW politics with no election-specific developments. The main items are government-side: the Minns government has scrapped the bring-your-own-laptop requirement in schools, has announced $5.2 million for two aerial ladder trucks for Sydney firefighters, and is facing renewed scrutiny of mental health care in the prison system following an ABC investigation. A NSW parliamentary inquiry is also examining regulation of combat sports.

stories.headline: Prisons psychiatrist says NSW Corrections failing mentally ill inmates
stories.summary: The ABC reports that, following its investigation into the care of prisoners with mental illness, a leading forensic psychiatrist has argued Corrections NSW should have no role in managing inmates' mental health. The ABC describes its investigation as having revealed systemic failures in that care.

stories.headline: Minns pulls the plug on BYO laptop to school
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports that the Minns government has dumped the bring-your-own-laptop rule for schools. No further detail was available in the supplied text.

stories.headline: $5.2 million boost to firefighting capability for growing Sydney
stories.summary: The NSW government says it is spending $5.2 million on two new high-tech aerial ladder trucks, which it says will improve firefighters' ability to respond to major fires and complex rescues as Sydney grows. The announcement was made in a ministerial release.

stories.headline: Stricter regulation on the cards for controversial combat sports
stories.summary: A NSW parliamentary inquiry is examining bare-knuckle boxing, collision running and competitive slapping, the ABC reports. Organisers of the sports have indicated they would work with authorities on regulation so the events can continue.

elsewhere.text: The Tally Room notes the Victorian Electoral Commission is progressively publishing candidate names ahead of Monday's close of nominations, with some Labor upper house MPs shifting regions.
